title: Minimal SaaS demo
summary: Product hierarchy with sample issue, ticket, incident, and a link. SLA policy configuration is handled via UI guidance.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Optional: sprint boards
steps: Open DevRev and navigate to your sprint or curated iteration view.
Assign one or more demo issues to a sprint if your story requires it.
Note: automated sprint discovery in this CLI aggregates sprint metadata from works.list responses and may miss empty sprints.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Configure SLA policies (UI only)
steps: Log in to your DevRev org and open the Settings area (gear / admin panel).
Locate the 'SLAs' or 'Service Level Agreements' section within Settings — this is managed entirely through the UI and is not currently available via the public REST API.
Create a new SLA policy by clicking 'Add policy' (or equivalent). Give it a descriptive name such as 'Demo P1 SLA' so it is easy to identify during the POC.
Define target response and resolution times for each priority tier (e.g. P1: 1 h response / 4 h resolution; P2: 4 h / 24 h). Adjust to match your prospect's expectations.
Set breach and warning thresholds (e.g. warn at 75 % of elapsed time) so the demo can visually show an SLA approaching breach.
Optionally configure business-hours calendars and holiday schedules under the same Settings area before saving the policy.

Associate the SLA policy with the relevant ticket queue or customer segment (e.g. apply to all tickets tagged with your demo account) so the tickets created in steps work-6 are governed by the policy.
Verify the policy is active by opening the demo ticket (work-6) and confirming the SLA timer is visible on the ticket detail view.
Refer to https://devrev.ai/docs/DevRevU/demos and https://developer.devrev.ai/beta/about/for-developers for the latest UI navigation details, as menu paths may change between releases.

steps.title: Create product: Acme Platform
steps.rationale: Blueprint part — establishes the top-level product node in the part hierarchy, giving every downstream capability, feature, and work item a coherent parent for the demo story.

steps.title: Create capability: Core Services
steps.rationale: Blueprint part (parent ref: prod:acme) — groups related features under a logical capability, demonstrating the multi-level part hierarchy to prospects.

steps.title: Create feature: SSO
steps.rationale: Blueprint part (parent ref: cap:core) — provides a concrete, recognisable feature that tickets, issues, and incidents will be attached to throughout the demo.

steps.title: Create enhancement: Onboarding checklist
steps.rationale: Blueprint part (parent ref: feat:sso) — illustrates the enhancement type within the part hierarchy, showing how product improvements are tracked alongside features.

steps.title: Create issue: Demo issue — backlog grooming
steps.rationale: Blueprint work ref=iss:demo1 — seeds the engineering backlog with a realistic issue tied to the SSO feature, enabling sprint and prioritisation storytelling.

steps.title: Create ticket: Demo ticket — customer question
steps.rationale: Blueprint work ref=tic:demo1 — represents an inbound customer support request against the SSO feature, anchoring the support-to-engineering traceability narrative.

steps.title: Create incident: Demo incident — brief outage
steps.rationale: Blueprint incident ref=inc:demo1 — introduces an operational event tied to the SSO feature so that the demo can show end-to-end incident → ticket → issue traceability.

steps.title: Link ticket → issue (is_related_to)
steps.rationale: Relates the customer-facing ticket to the engineering issue, demonstrating bidirectional traceability between support and product development in the demo.

steps.title: Link incident → ticket (is_related_to)
steps.rationale: Associates the incident with the customer ticket so reviewers can trace the operational outage back to a specific support request, completing the incident-to-ticket-to-issue chain.
